newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares put on late surge led by Fib futures.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares put on late surge led by Fib futures.

text.p: Italian stocks surged in late trading on Wednesday, boosted by gains on Wall Street, and led higher by Fib bourse index futures with the September contract posting a closing gain of 4.39 percent to 22,840 after a peak at 22,850.
"The future broke a series of technical resistance points one after the other and the market took off, getting out of the oversold situation seen in recent sessions," one dealer said.
The all-share Mibtel index ended up 2.56 percent at 14,691 after a 14,696 high and the Mib30 blue chip index closed 2.96 percent higher at a 22,296 session high.

There was a return of buying interest seen for a series of recently neglected shares. Energy group ENI rose 3.02 percent to 10,665 lire, Montedison put on 5.37 percent to 1,178, insurer Generali rose 3.59 percent to 35,683 and Credito Italiano bank gained 5.2 percent to 3,498.
Traded volume was seen good at some 1.3 trillion lire.
Operators said the market was comforted by signs of less tension on the interest rate front following higher than expected German July jobless data.
The market was also looking ahead to options expiry on Thursday of next week.

Montedison's energy arm Edison performed well throughout the day after the government ruled this week private electricity producers could sell excess capacity to third parties after state utility Enel said it will no longer be buying the excess supplies. Edison ended 5.45 percent higher at 8,457 lire.
Food group Parmalat put on 3.72 percent to 2,596 lire after a buy recommendation from Credit Suisse First Boston.
Tyre and cable-maker Pirelli SpA gained 3.97 percent to 4,972 and Fiat gained 0.63 percent to 5,933.
